text.p: Ford Motor Co. ordered a recall of 637,000 Explorer and Mountaineer sport utility vehicles Thursday, mostly for a minor problem with a power mirror but some for an icing problem that may race the engine.

The recall from the second-largest U.S. automaker also included 1,697 model-year 1998 F700 and F800 trucks and B800 school buses. A weld in the transmission system may be suspect and could allow the vehicles to roll when placed in "park," or confuse drivers about the gear.
The recall for the engine problem on the sport utility vehicles was directed at 27,000 of its 1996 and 1997 Explorers and 1997 Mountaineers equipped with 5.0-litre engines.

It said that ice could form in the throttle body of the vehicles during prolonged highway travel in the cold. The ice could prevent the throttle plate from closing and prevent the engine from returning to idle.
Of the vehicles affected, 4,000 were in Canada and the remainder in Northern states, Ford said.
The mirror problem affected electrical circuits on 610,000 1993 and 1994 Explorers, 25,000 of them in Canada.
"The power mirror switch could experience an internal short circuit, creating the potential for overheating in the driver-side door," the company said in a statement explaining the problem.
Ford was notifying affected owners by mail and asked them to return their vehicles to dealers for inspection and appropriate repairs -- free of charge.
Ford stock fell 50 cents to $38.25 in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
